title: Prediction Models for Delayed Bleeding After Colorectal Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Prediction Models for Delayed Bleeding After Colorectal Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Background · deo270456-sec-0050-p3】Therefore, this systematic review aims to systematically retrieve, evaluate, and synthesize the existing research evidence on predictive models for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD. By comprehensively assessing their methodological design, predictive performance, strengths, and limitations, and clarifying their applicable scenarios based on the timing of predictor availability, this review provides evidence‐based references for clinicians to select optimal predictive tools, while also identifying directions for further optimizing models and developing standardized, clinically feasible tools.

【Background · deo270456-sec-0050-p1】Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) has become a standard minimally invasive technique for the treatment of early colorectal cancer and precancerous lesions. Its advantage lies in enabling en bloc resection of lesions, with reported en bloc resection rates ranging from 89.2% to 92.5% [1, 2, 3]. Compared with conventional surgery, ESD offers less trauma, faster recovery, and shorter hospital stays [4]. However, the technical complexity of colorectal ESD—characterized by high difficulty, prolonged operation time, and submucosal dissection—increases the risk of vascular and muscular injury [5]. Consequently, complications are not entirely avoidable. Among these, delayed bleeding is one of the most common complications, clinically manifesting as melena or hematochezia after the procedure and, in severe cases, can lead to hemorrhagic shock. Its reported incidence ranges from 2.80% to 5.37% [6, 7], prolonging hospitalization, increasing costs, and threatening patient safety. Despite precise intraoperative hemostasis and prophylactic interventions, the lack of effective risk assessment tools prevents targeted individualized management for high‐risk patients, contributing to the recurrent occurrence of delayed bleeding [8].

sections.text:

【Study Design · deo270456-sec-0070-p1】This systematic review was prospectively registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews prior to the commencement of literature searches (Registration ID: CRD420251252241).

【Methods · abstract-2-1】We searched five databases through March 2026 for observational studies that developed or validated prediction models or scoring systems for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD in adults (≥18 years). Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using PROBAST.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Prediction Models for Delayed Bleeding After Colorectal Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Conclusion · deo270456-sec-0210-p1】In summary, our systematic review identified five studies describing five predictive models for delayed bleeding in colorectal ESD patients. There are a limited number of models for delayed bleeding in colorectal ESD patients of all ages. The most commonly used predictors were lesion location and lesion size. Discrimination in derivation cohorts ranged from 0.726 to 0.890, internal validation AUCs ranged from 0.739 to 0.870, and the externally validated model achieved an AUC of 0.634. According to PROBAST, all five included studies that developed or validated predictive models were evaluated as having a high risk of bias (with low concerns regarding applicability), and therefore require cautious interpretation.

【Results · abstract-3-1】Of 25,177 records screened, five studies reporting five predictive models were included. The incidence of delayed bleeding ranged from 2.9% to 9.9%. The most commonly used predictors were lesion location and lesion size. Discrimination in derivation cohorts ranged from 0.726 to 0.890, internal validation areas under the curve [AUCs] ranged from 0.739 to 0.870, and the externally validated model achieved an AUC of 0.634. All studies were judged to have a high risk of bias, mainly because of inadequate reporting in the predictor, outcome, and analysis domains, although most had low concerns regarding applicability.
